hypothesis: A fail-open deterministic post-rerank compatibility fallback will reduce explicit execution/control/bore conflicts by substituting only an already retrieved, fully evidenced compatible candidate.
why_now: Current evidence points to final-selection conflicts rather than retrieval misses; this is a materially different, bounded alternative to prior broad gating, prompt changes, and index enrichment.
expected_effect: Correct unsafe top selections while preserving the reranker outcome when no compatible, evidenced alternative exists.
expected_metric_gain: +3.3–10 pp public hard-pass; +0–6.7 pp blind hard-pass.
lesson_from_history: Cycle 1 broad filtering and Cycle 5 prompt-based selection changes regressed. This design never filters before reranking, uses literal deterministic cues, and falls back only to an existing compatible candidate. Cycle 7 index enrichment regressed, so no rebuild is requested.
candidate_hypotheses: Catalog-side index enrichment or RRF tuning.
plan_summary: Created and strict-validated proposal, spec, design, and implementation-only tasks at openspec/changes/cycle-08-verifiable-selection-fallback/. No product code was changed.
